name: CamJam
description: A tiny, low-bandwidth webcam feed for a space: a stop-motion camera share rather than a video call. One member at a time shares their webcam as a small JPEG still, sent on an interval and fanned out live to everyone watching, captioned with the sharer's name and how long ago the still was taken. A still every few seconds costs a fraction of a video call and reads as presence rather than surveillance. Cadence and detail are one owner setting that moves them together, from a 100px thumbnail twice a second up to a 1920px still once a minute. Any member, viewers included, can start sharing, pick which camera to use, take over an active feed or rename the feed in place; only a member who presses share is ever asked for their camera. Nothing is recorded: the current still lives in memory on the keeper's device and disappears when sharing stops, and there is no microphone or audio. Who can watch follows the space's own sharing: members, and anyone the space lets in when the frame is published.
